pass_a_gloss: A great theatre is being clapped together over you who are contending and being called to the martyrdom, as if we were saying such a thing happens over some contestants reckoned wonderful, with countless numbers assembling for the sight of the contest. And you will say not less than Paul when you contend: we became a theatre for the world and messengers and humans. So the whole world and all the messengers, right and left, and all humans, both those from the share of God and those from the others, will hear us contending the contest about Christianity. And either the messengers in heavens will be glad over us, and streams will clap with hand at the same time, and the hills will leap for joy, and every timber of the plain will clap with the boughs; or, which may it not be, also the powers beneath that are glad at evil will be glad. And nothing is out of place to see from the things written by Isaiah the things that will be said by those in Hades to those who have been conquered and have fallen down from the heavenly witness, so that we may shiver yet more at the impiety in disowning. For I suppose that such things will be said toward the one who has disowned: Hades from beneath was made bitter having met you; together all the giants were raised for you, those who ruled the earth, those who roused out of their thrones all kings of nations; all will reply and speak to you. And what will the conquered powers speak to those conquered, and those taken by the devil to those taken in disowning, what then are these? you also were taken as also we, and among us you were reckoned. And if someone, obtaining a great hope and glorious, the one in God, by cowardice or by toils brought on is worsted in God, he will hear: your glory went down into Hades, your much good cheer; under you they will strew rot, and your covering a grub. And if someone also gleamed in the assemblies often as the light bearer appearing to them, with his fine deeds gleaming in front of humans, and after these things, contending the great contest, has ruined the wreath of such a throne, he will hear: how did the light bearer, the one rising early, drop out of heaven? he was smashed upon the earth. And this also will be said toward him, made similar to the devil through the disowning: you will be flung in the hills one dead body loathed, with many who have died, stabbed through with blades, going down into Hades; in what manner a cloak mixed up in blood will not be pure, so neither will you be pure. For how will he be pure, stained with blood and killing, the loathsome stumble of disowning, and kneaded together with so great an evil? Now let us show that we heard the: the one fond of son or daughter over me is not deserving of me; let us attend, lest perhaps even a hesitation about whether ever one must disown or must acknowledge comes about in us, so that the word of Elijah may not be said also toward us, holding so: until when will you limp upon both the hams; if the lord is God, walk behind him.
pass_b_english: A great theatre is gathering to watch you as you contend and are called to martyrdom, just as if we were to say that this happens with certain contenders thought to be marvels, when countless thousands gather to see the contest. And when you contend, you will say no less than Paul did: “We have become a theatre to the world, to angels and to human beings” (1 Corinthians 4:9). So the whole world and all the angels, of the right and of the left, and all human beings, both those of God's portion and those of the rest, will hear us as we contend in the contest for Christianity. And either the angels in heaven will rejoice over us, and “the rivers will clap their hands together, and the mountains will exult” (Psalm 98:8), “and all the trees of the field will clap with their branches” (Isaiah 55:12); or, may it not be so, the powers below too, who delight in evil, will rejoice.

There is nothing out of place in seeing, from what is written in Isaiah, the words that those in Hades will speak to the ones who have been defeated and have fallen from the heavenly martyrdom, so that we may shudder all the more at the impiety of denial. For I think that such things will be said to the one who has denied: “Hades below was embittered when it met you; all the giants who ruled the earth rose up together for you, those who raised all the kings of the nations from their thrones. All of them will answer and say to you” (Isaiah 14:9-10). And what will the defeated powers say to the defeated, and those whom the devil has captured to those captured in denial? What, then, are these words? “You too were captured, just as we were, and you were counted among us” (Isaiah 14:10). And if someone who had a great and glorious hope in God is defeated in God through cowardice or through the pains brought on him, he will hear: “Your glory has gone down to Hades, your great gladness; beneath you they will spread decay, and the worm will be your covering” (Isaiah 14:11).

And if someone has often shone in the churches, appearing to them like “the morning star” while his good works shone “before men” (Matthew 5:16), and afterwards, in contending the great contest, has lost the crown of so great a throne, he will hear: “How has the morning star, which rose at dawn, fallen from heaven? He has been crushed upon the earth” (Isaiah 14:12). And this too will be said to him who through denial has become like the devil: “You will be cast out on the mountains, a corpse abhorred, with many dead who were pierced through with swords, going down to Hades. As a garment soaked in blood will not be clean, so neither will you be clean” (Isaiah 14:19-20). For how will one be clean who has been defiled with blood and murder, the abominable fall of denial, and steeped in so great an evil?

Now let us show that we have heard the words “He who loves son or daughter above me is not worthy of me” (Matthew 10:37). Let us take care that not even a doubt arises in us as to whether we should deny or confess, so that the word of Elijah, which runs like this, may not be spoken to us too: “How long will you go lame on both your knees? If the Lord is God, go after him” (1 Kings 18:21).

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 18); the old English was a digest. The old English invented much of this chapter ('God the president', 'saints rejoicing', 'Choose then before whom to contend nobly'), added 'but if Baal' to Elijah's words, and dropped Isaiah 14:10-12, 14:19-20 and Origen's comments.
Koetschau calls it a scribal error from the preceding word and conjectures συναθροιζομένων; translated 'gather'.
x τῶν read ἐκ τῶν; apveloϑαι read ἀρνεῖσθαι; οδιφήσῃ read ῥιφήσῃ ('you will be cast'); καθα006 read καθαρός; ἔστε μου ἄξιος read ἔστι μου ἄξιος; xav read κἄν; ἕνα read ἵνα.
Printed εἷς where the Greek Isaiah has ὡς; rendered 'a corpse abhorred', which stands for either reading.
'Theatre', not 'spectacle', to keep Origen's link with the 'great theatre' of the opening line.
'Knees' (the hollow of the knee) in 1 Kings 18:21.
'Has lost the crown of so great a throne'.
